title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang
short: Cloudflare: one customer's reply decoded from others' KV cache
author: Kevin Flansburg, Michelle Chen (Cloudflare)
more_note: Its diagram of the healthy and the rejected handoff (eight pages, the two admission queues) is worth opening there; this page redraws it as a step animation with a third, fixed mode.

companion.t: SGLang security update: improving request isolation
companion.n: The engine maintainers' half of the coordinated disclosure, published the same day: the admission fix in their words, and most of it on the related race (an aborted transfer's late RDMA writes landing in reused slots), its deterministic reproduction, deferred release, checksums and their measured cost.

takeaway: From 27 August to 9 September 2026, Workers AI's GLM-5.3 endpoint advertised a 1,048,576-token window on a 681,280-token prefill KV pool; prompts over the pool took SGLang's rejection path, which in disaggregated mode still handed decode one token of cache, and decode answered from reserved pages still holding earlier requests' data. Cloudflare counts 155 affected responses; the fix enlarged the pool and retires rejected requests before the handoff, as SGLang's main branch already did two days before the report.
verdict: Believe the mechanism and the fix: SGLang's own source, pull requests and companion post confirm every step. Read 155 as a count of affected replies, method unstated, saying nothing about whose data surfaced; and note that the mismatch was known before launch and the bug public since 6 July.

headline.k: 27 August to 9 September 2026, all to prompts over 681,280 tokens
headline.d: Cloudflare's count; no sign of deliberate exploitation

headline.k: behind a 1,048,576-token context window: 65% of what the window promised
headline.d: sized from memory the weights leave free, not from the window
headline.at: the KV cache pool on our prefill GPUs only had room for 681,280 tokens

headline.k: the prefill pool after the fix, about twice the window
headline.d: plus an engine patch that refuses before the KV handoff
headline.at: the prefill KV pool now holds about 2.04 million tokens

discussion.t: Hacker News: "Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)"

responses.t: SGLang security update: improving request isolation
responses.n: Agrees on the mechanism and credits #36988 with the fix; declined the transferred-length check Cloudflare proposed (both sides compute the length from the same prefill accounting) and judged prefill's source pages already safe. The researcher's report, "available soon", was not found by 27 November.

responses.t: We name the model because customers need to know which endpoint was affected
responses.by: kflansburg (Kevin Flansburg, an author), Hacker News
responses.n: The post never blames the model; it names it so customers know which endpoint was hit. The title was not changed.

responses.t: An expected error that came back as success should have been investigated
responses.n: Success where an error was expected should itself have been investigated; the post concedes its tests checked status and speed only.

responses.t: A normal multi-turn 1M session would work fine
responses.n: Says only single prefills over 681k were hit. Wrong by SGLang's code: the check counts the whole prompt, cached or not.

responses.t: Were the customers whose data leaked told?
responses.n: Million-token prompts often carry whole repositories and secrets; the post does not say whether the exposed customers were identified or told.

responses.t: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
responses.by: Niranjan Deshpande and David Africa, LessWrong
responses.n: Not a reply: on working engines, SGLang included, a shared prefix cache lets two models signal through numerical fingerprints (1,221 of 1,221 games with a fine-tuned reader). Per-user cache isolation closes it.

since_label: the engine and the fix, checked 27 November 2026

since.t: PR #45973: failed NIXL and MORI sends no longer acknowledged as drained
since.n: The last fix in SGLang's disclosure timeline, merged 23 October and listed in the v0.5.23 release notes (2 November): the race's protection for the two transfer backends #43719 did not cover.

since.t: Draft #46435: optionally zero KV pages on free
since.n: Opened by Kevin Flansburg on 25 October (an opt-in flag that zeroes freed pages, so a read of a page a request does not own returns zeros, not another request's KV; MLA and DSA pools only) and closed unmerged on 17 November. No merged zero-on-free by 27 November.

since.t: Cloudflare's #38704: honor admission aborts before KV handoff
since.n: Closed unmerged on 10 October; #38935 took its admission approach, and the transferred-length check it added was declined upstream.

resources.t: Issue #30233: aborted prefill requests (input too long) cause decode to generate garbage from incomplete KV cache
resources.n: The same bug, reported seven weeks before the launch on a GLM-5.2 deployment with a 1,048,576-token context and a 284,928-token pool, with the root cause traced line by line and a proposed patch; closed for inactivity on 5 September.

resources.t: PR #36988: Retire aborted disaggregated prefill results
resources.n: Written for a failing vision encoder, not this incident; it retires an aborted request when its prefill result returns, so its stub KV never reaches decode. The change that stops the exposure, released in v0.5.20 on 18 September.

resources.t: PR #38935: Do not admit intake-rejected requests to a PD handoff
resources.n: Retires a rejected request at both admission doors. Its description calls itself "a waste-and-latency fix, not a correctness fix": after #36988 the stale-KV symptom no longer reproduced on main. Its tests cover the doors, re-entering preempted requests, and single-node mode left alone.

resources.t: Smaller, faster, safer: running Kimi and GLM at scale
resources.n: The earlier post describing the disaggregated GLM deployment and the page-tag integrity check (under 1% overhead), which the incident post says was disabled after mid-August tests.

resources.t: Cloudflare status: Workers AI increased errors
resources.n: The public notice during the incident: investigating at 14:25 UTC, identified at 15:02, resolved at 20:09; it speaks of errors on GLM 5.3, not of data exposure.

resources.t: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
resources.n: The transfer engine between Cloudflare's prefill and decode pools, and the design it comes from.

kb.t: Batching, KV cache and scheduling in depth
kb.n: Owns paged attention, the block pool and its free list, admission and preemption: the machinery whose bookkeeping failed here.
Owns splitting prefill from decode and the KV transfer between them (section 6), the handoff this bug went through.

kb.t: SGLang: radix cache, cache-aware scheduling, large-scale serving
kb.n: Owns SGLang as a system: its pool flags (--mem-fraction-static, --max-total-tokens), transfer backends and versions.

kb.t: Long context: KV cache growth and compression
kb.n: Owns KV cache sizing: why a million-token window needs a pool that large, and what it costs per token.

kb.t: Agent security: permissions, sandboxes, prompt injection, egress
kb.n: Owns the agent's threat model; this incident sits one layer below it, in the shared inference server every agent's prompts pass through.
